core_obligations: Set up the induction on the number r of generators of the finite module M (proof line 709-710).

Peel off one generator: let M' = Rx_1, note that M/M' has r - 1 generators so the induction hypothesis yields a filtration there, and identify M' with R/I_1 for I_1 = {f : f x_1 = 0} (proof lines 710-714).

Assemble the filtration: the preimage of the filtration of M/M' together with the submodule M' gives a filtration 0 = M_0 subset ... subset M_n = M whose successive quotients are the cyclic modules of the induction plus R/I_1 (statement and the two steps above).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the number of generators, splitting off the cyclic submodule generated by the first generator (proof lines 709-713).
Read the quotients of the resulting filtration as quotients of R by ideals (proof lines 713-714).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every finite module over a ring admits a filtration whose successive quotients are isomorphic to R modulo some ideal, that is, are cyclic (statement lines 694-707, whose slogan records the one-line content). The proof is an induction on the number of generators: the submodule generated by one generator is cyclic and hence of the form R/I_1, the quotient by it has one generator fewer so the induction hypothesis applies, and the two filtrations combine (proof lines 709-714). The step that carries the content is the bookkeeping of the induction, since both ingredients are immediate; the author writes it out in full. H2.
